**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A 5-*juàn* Sòng *bǐjì* by [馬永卿](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E6%B0%B8%E5%8D%BF), the disciple-recorder of [劉安世](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%96) (Liú Ānshì, 1048–1125). The book is paired in transmission with Mǎ's *Yuánchéng yǔ lù* ([KR3j0102](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0102)); like the *Yǔ lù* it preserves a substantial body of Liú Ānshì's talk, and through Liú a body of [司馬光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E5%85%89)'s (Sīmǎ Guāng's) transmitted teaching to which Liú gave first claim. The book itself is *bǐjì* in form — a free-running record of textual *kǎozhèng*, anecdotal *bǐjì*-jottings, and reflections — and is the more philological of Mǎ's two surviving works. The colophon dates the compilation to *Shàoxīng* 6 (1136), making it the later of his two books.

**Abstract**

The *Lǎn zhēn zǐ* — the title from the author's self-style "Idle-but-True Master" — is Mǎ Yǒngqīng's miscellaneous *bǐjì*, completed at *Shàoxīng* 6 (1136) by the colophon date. The book is the principal philological monument of the [劉安世](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%96) school and an important witness for late-Northern-Sòng / early-Southern-Sòng textual scholarship.

In content the book is mixed. The major elements are: (a) *kǎozhèng* on classical texts (*Shū*, *Shī*, *Hàn shū*, *Zhuāng zǐ*) — generally exact and oft-cited by later philologists; (b) Sòng *bǐjì* anecdotes, especially those preserving the recorded speech of [司馬光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E5%85%89) (Sīmǎ Guāng) and [劉安世](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%96); (c) opening entries on Sīmǎ Guāng, a continuation of Mǎ's role as a transmitter of the Wēngōng tradition; (d) reflections on contemporary politics, the *Yuányòu* / *Shàoshèng* factional struggle, and the post-*Jìngkāng* southern migration; (e) some *chán*-flavoured speculation, deriving from Liú Ānshì's known interest in *chán* — for which the *Sìkù* editors apologise.

The book's three most-cited refutations — by Yuán Wén 袁文, Wáng Mào 王楙, and Fèi Gǔn 費袞 ([KR3j0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0121)) — are themselves a witness to its sustained Southern Sòng circulation. The book is not registered in Cháo Gōngwǔ's *Jùnzhāi dúshū zhì* or Chén Zhènsūn's *Zhízhāi shūlù jiětí*; the *Sìkù* editors regard this as an oversight, citing the running refutations as proof of the book's general currency in Southern Sòng.

Dating. The colophon dates compilation to *Shàoxīng* 6 (1136), one year after the prefaces to the companion *Yǔ lù*. Author lifedates are not precisely known; CBDB id 33866 records *fl.* 1109 (the *jìnshì* date).

The standard text is the SKQS recension. A modern edition is in the Sòng-Yuán bǐjì cóngkān series (Zhōnghuá shūjú).
